fields.h1: Build a Local Business Landing Page That Takes Orders
fields.hero_description: Build a local business landing page with your hours and address up top, and every order saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Local Page
fields.features_subheading: A local business landing page shows nearby visitors where you are, when you open, and how to book. Emergent builds one by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from your description

Describe the shop and the streets you cover. Emergent builds the page around it, with your opening times and address set above an order or booking form. Prompt to change any part.
fields.feature_2:
Every order saved as a row

Each order or booking lands as a row in a database you own, with the customer's name and the time they picked. Sort the rows by day before the doors open on a busy Saturday.
fields.feature_3:
A heads-up when someone books

The app sends a Slack or email alert to whoever runs the counter the moment a booking arrives. Add a reminder for the customer that goes out on the evening before the visit.
fields.feature_4:
Limits the page holds to

Tell Emergent the limit, such as 12 orders per pickup slot or one client per stylist at a time. The page stops offering a time once it is taken, and nobody needs to watch it.
fields.feature_5:
Connected to the tools you run

Built apps connect to any tool with an API, such as Stripe or HubSpot, and sync data in and out. A new customer from the page can land in the contact list you already keep.
fields.feature_6:
Your street address, your web address

Publish the page on your own domain, such as yourshop.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
All 4 pickup slots close at 12 orders

Fenwick Bakehouse takes Saturday pre-orders in 4 pickup slots, one each hour. A slot leaves the page once it holds 12 orders. This week 41 orders came in: the 8:00 and 9:00 slots filled, 10:00 took 10, and 11:00 took 7. Ines Barcelo ordered a sourdough loaf and 6 morning buns for 10:00.
fields.tab_content_2:
For each stylist, only their open times show

A visitor to Larkspur Salon picks a stylist first, and the page shows that stylist's open times and nobody else's. Theo Castellanos chose Saffi Ondrejka and booked a 90-minute color at 2:30 on Thursday. The app saved the booking and emailed it to Saffi, who has 3 open times left that day.
fields.tab_content_3:
Repairs from 6 neighborhoods ride in the van

Ruefield Cycles sends its van for repairs in 6 neighborhoods near the shop. A visitor enters an address, and the page offers free van pickup inside those 6 and a drop-off time everywhere else. Of 26 repair requests in October, 19 got van pickup and 7 got drop-off. Ottoline Pryce in Kestle Row was picked up on a Tuesday.
fields.tab_content_4:
One prompt set holiday hours on 3 location pages

Thistledown Coffee runs three shops, and each has a page of its own with the address and opening times beside a map link. One prompt, "Close at 2:00 on Thanksgiving at every shop," changed the hours on all 3 pages. The Haskett Avenue page now lists Thanksgiving as 7:00 to 2:00.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Local Business Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a local business landing page that answers a nearby visitor's first questions and saves every order or booking.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose the one action for the page
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the address and hours up top
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one thing a nearby visitor should do: order for pickup, book a chair, or request a repair. Build the page around that action. Links to the menu, the story of the shop, and gift cards can sit lower down.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the address and hours where a phone shows them without scrolling. Match the hours on your Google business profile. Google's help page for profiles lists your business hours, including special store hours, among the details to keep up to date. A visitor should never find two answers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each limit down as a number before you prompt: orders per pickup slot, bookings per stylist per day, how far the van goes. A number becomes a rule the page can hold. A phrase like busy Saturdays gives the page nothing to enforce.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the business to Emergent in plain words, with what you sell and the limits from step 3. Emergent builds the page and a table for every entry its form takes. Read the draft as a customer would, then prompt changes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Give each location its own page
fields.howto_step_5_des: If you run more than one shop, give each one its own page with its address and directions. Keep one shared menu or price list that every location page reads from. A visitor near one shop should not scroll past the other two.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask three regular customers for one sentence each about what they bought, and add their first names. Use photos of your actual counter or workbench in place of stock images. Show a visitor choosing between two shops on one street what yours looks like inside.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place a test order or booking on your phone, then check the new row in your database and the alert that reached the counter. Change the hours once by prompt and confirm every page shows the new times before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a local business landing page?
faq_plan.a: A local business landing page is a single web page for a business with a physical address, written for people nearby. It puts the address and hours in the first screen and asks for one action, such as an order for pickup or a booking.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a local business landing page?
faq_plan.a: Decide the one action the page asks for, then describe the business and its limits to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the page with its booking form and the database each entry lands in. Change any part of it later by prompt.

faq_plan.q: Which details belong in the first screen of a local business landing page?
faq_plan.hint: What content to include on a local business landing page?
faq_plan.a: The address and hours, beside the main button. Below them, add what you sell with prices. Real photos of the shop and a few customer reviews come next. Emergent builds the order form too, and each entry lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How is a local business landing page different from a homepage?
faq_plan.a: A homepage introduces the whole business; a local business landing page serves people in one place and asks them for one action. A shop with one location can use it as its homepage. A business landing page aimed at buyers anywhere leads with the offer, not the address and hours.

faq_plan.q: Should a business with several locations make a local business landing page for each one?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the locations differ in opening times or in what they offer. Each page then carries one set of details a visitor can trust. Keep shared content, such as the menu, in one place that every page reads from. With Emergent, one prompt can change the hours on every location page.

faq_plan.q: How do I show holiday hours on a local business landing page?
faq_plan.a: List them on the page a week ahead, beside the regular hours, with the day named. If the page carries LocalBusiness structured data, Google's documentation says to use both the validFrom and validThrough properties to define seasonal hours. Change your business profile on the same day, and check that the two agree.

faq_plan.q: How many form fields does a local business landing page need?
faq_plan.a: Only the ones it takes to fill the order or booking: a name and phone number, plus the item and the time. A b2b landing page may ask for company size and role because a sales team follows up. A bakery only needs to know who is coming and when.

faq_plan.q: Can a local business landing page help a shop show up in local search?
faq_plan.a: It can help, though it is only part of the picture. Google's help page says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity. On the page itself, name what you sell and the neighborhood you serve in plain words. Keep the address and hours the same as on your business profile.

faq_plan.q: Should a local business landing page use structured data?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you want search engines to read your details in a set format. Google's documentation says you can tell Google about business hours, different departments within a business, and other details with Local Business structured data. Mark up the same address and hours the page shows.

faq_plan.q: What call to action works best on a local business landing page?
faq_plan.a: Name the action on the button itself, such as Reserve a table or Get a pickup time, in place of Submit. Put it in the first screen and again after the reviews. A service landing page for work done at the customer's address asks for a quote; a shop asks for a visit or an order.

plan.angle: The top 10 for local business landing page are SEO guides to location pages and design galleries: they say what a local page should carry but never hand over a working one. This page shows four local business pages built from a prompt, each doing the one job a nearby visitor came for: a bakery's Saturday pre-orders that close each pickup slot at 12 orders, a salon page that shows one stylist's open times, a bike shop that offers van pickup only in 6 neighborhoods, and a coffee shop with one page per location whose holiday hours change by one prompt. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, what to include, hours and address, one page per location, reviews, how Google ranks local results, phones, holiday hours and the call to action. Contractor, plumber, HVAC, roofing, chiropractic, dentist, fitness and service pages are siblings and stay out.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Local Business Landing Page That Takes Orders' and hero 'with your hours and address up top, and every order saved to a database you own' cover the whole job for a storefront business.

intent.evidence: Top 10 are local-page guides and example galleries; page gives four built examples (bakery, salon, bike shop, multi-location cafe), a 7-step how-to and FAQ on hours, locations, structured data and local ranking.

specificity.evidence: 'A slot leaves the page once it holds 12 orders'; 'free van pickup inside those 6 and a drop-off time everywhere else'; table variant 'Prompt for a campaign page'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Fenwick Bakehouse takes Saturday pre-orders...', 'Write down the one thing a nearby visitor should do'.

craft.evidence: Sentences one idea each; QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean.

voice.evidence: 'A number becomes a rule the page can hold. A phrase like busy Saturdays gives the page nothing to enforce.'

truth.evidence: All four Google statements match their domain_sources quotes and scope: 'mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity' (GBP 7091), 'business hours, including special store hours' (GBP 7091), 'business hours, different departments within a business' and 'use both the validFrom and validThrough properties to define seasonal hours' (LocalBusiness docs). Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts (reminders included), api-connect, custom-domain, code-export; 'Free to start' is the approved free-start claim. Tab numbers add up: 12+12+10+7=41, 19+7=26.

distinct.evidence: Storefront segments (bakery, salon, bike shop, cafe) do not overlap the home-service siblings (service, hvac, plumber, roofing, contractor) or chiropractic's clinic tabs; FAQ contrasts and links business-landing-page, b2b-landing-page and service-landing-page instead of answering their topics.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first, no brands in questions; hub link in item 2; 3 sibling links with exact-match anchors.
